After a successful buyShares call, _BASE_TARGET_ must equal 1001 plus the base input amount.
After a successful buyShares call, _BASE_TARGET_ must equal 1001 plus the base input amount.
After a buyShares call that initializes the pool, _BASE_TARGET_ must equal 1001 plus the base input amount.

After any call to adjustMtFeeRate, _BASE_TARGET_ should equal _BASE_RESERVE_ whenever _RState_ is ONE, but the buggy version may leave _BASE_TARGET_ stale when transitioning from BELOW_ONE without resetting it.

After adjustMtFeeRate is called, the PMMState should satisfy that if RState is ONE then BASE_TARGET equals BASE_RESERVE and QUOTE_TARGET equals QUOTE_RESERVE; the buggy version violates this invariant when a BELOW_ONE->ONE transition is triggered by correctRState via adjustMtFeeRate without resetting BASE_TARGET.

After calling adjustMtFeeRate, if BASE_TARGET_ is strictly greater than BASE_RESERVE_ but RState_ is ONE, the buggy version fails to set BASE_TARGET_ equal to BASE_RESERVE_, while the reference version guarantees they are equal.

After calling adjustMtFeeRate, if the state is BELOW_ONE and _BASE_RESERVE_ < _BASE_TARGET_, the reference contract correctly sets _BASE_TARGET_ to _BASE_RESERVE_ during the transition to ONE, while the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged (stale and greater than _BASE_RESERVE_), violating the invariant that in state ONE, _BASE_TARGET_ equals _BASE_RESERVE_.

After any call to adjustMtFeeRate(...), if a transition from BELOW_ONE to ONE occurs in correctRState, the reference resets _BASE_TARGET_ to _BASE_RESERVE_, while the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged, so when RState_ is ONE, c._BASE_TARGET_() must equal c._BASE_RESERVE_() for the reference but may differ for the bug.
When the state is ABOVE_ONE, the base target is never less than the base reserve after correctRState() is called.
After buyShares when _BASE_TARGET_ changes, the new _BASE_TARGET_ equals the old _BASE_TARGET_ plus the minted portion, regardless of RState corrections.
